reference_answer: Kaplan et al. conclude that compute-optimal training uses very large models on relatively modest data; Chinchilla finds current models undertrained and that model size and tokens should be scaled equally.
key_facts: Kaplan: large models on modest data
Chinchilla: scale parameters and tokens equally

reference_answer: Wei et al. present emergent abilities as unpredictable effects of scale; Schaeffer et al. argue they appear because of nonlinear or discontinuous metrics and vanish with continuous metrics.
key_facts: Wei: emergence not predictable by extrapolation
Schaeffer: emergence is a metric artifact

reference_answer: Both lines of work favor retrieval: Ovadia et al. find RAG consistently outperforms unsupervised fine-tuning for existing and new knowledge, and Lewis et al. report RAG generates more factual language than a parametric-only baseline.
key_facts: RAG outperforms unsupervised fine-tuning
LLMs struggle to learn new facts via unsupervised fine-tuning

reference_answer: Both report that multi-query attention (shared keys/values) speeds decoding with some quality degradation; GQA uses an intermediate number of key-value heads to approach multi-head quality at MQA-like speed.
key_facts: MQA: minor quality degradation
GQA closes the quality gap with MHA

reference_answer: Rafailov et al. report DPO exceeds or matches PPO-based RLHF; Xu et al. argue DPO has fundamental limitations and PPO surpasses other alignment methods in all their testbeds.
key_facts: DPO paper: DPO >= PPO
Xu et al.: PPO surpasses DPO

reference_answer: GPTQ quantizes to 3-4 bits with negligible accuracy loss and the comprehensive evaluation finds 4-bit LLMs retain performance comparable to non-quantized ones.
key_facts: GPTQ: 3-4 bits negligible degradation
4-bit comparable to full precision

reference_answer: GPTQ reports end-to-end inference speedups over FP16 (about 3.25x-4.5x), while the comprehensive evaluation warns that quantization can also slow down inference.
key_facts: GPTQ: speedups over FP16
Evaluation study: quantization can slow inference

reference_answer: DPR reports dense retrieval beating BM25 by 9-19 points of top-20 accuracy in-domain, while BEIR finds BM25 a robust zero-shot baseline that dense models often underperform; E5 claims to be the first to beat BM25 on BEIR zero-shot without labeled data.
key_facts: DPR: dense > BM25 in-domain
BEIR: BM25 robust, dense often underperforms zero-shot

reference_answer: Min et al. find that randomly replacing demonstration labels barely hurts performance; Yoo et al. find label correctness can matter depending on configuration, and Wei et al. show large models can follow flipped labels, so labels matter at scale.
key_facts: Min: labels barely matter
Yoo / Wei: label correctness matters depending on setup and scale

reference_answer: Hu et al. report LoRA performs on par or better than fine-tuning; Biderman et al. find LoRA substantially underperforms full fine-tuning on programming and math, though it forgets less.
key_facts: LoRA paper: on par or better
LoRA Learns Less: substantially underperforms
